draft.title: Phylogenetic trees
card: A phylogenetic tree is a branching diagram that shows the evolutionary relationships between species or groups.
Each branch point (node) represents a common ancestor that the groups after it share. The tips of the branches show the species being compared.
Species that split from a node more recently share a more recent common ancestor. They are more closely related than species whose shared node is further back.
Closeness of relationship is read from how recent the shared node is, not from how near the tips sit on the page.
draft.remember: Read relatedness from the most recent shared branch point, not from how close the tips look.

a.q: On a phylogenetic tree, what does a branch point represent?
opts: A common ancestor of the groups that branch from it
A species that died out before the others
The species with the most advanced features
The point where two species became identical
a.why: A node is where a common ancestor split into separate lines. It is not a feature of any one species, and it does not mean species became identical.
a.clue: Think about what lies behind the split.

b.q: On a tree, species P and Q branch from a node. That node and species R branch from an older node. Which statement is correct?
opts: P is more closely related to Q than to R
P is more closely related to R than to Q
Q is more closely related to R than to P
P, Q and R are equally related to each other
b.why: P and Q share a more recent common ancestor with each other than either does with R. R only joins them at the older node, so R is more distantly related to both.
b.clue: Find which pair shares the most recent node.

a.best: A common ancestor of the groups that branch from it

b.best: P is more closely related to Q than to R
